text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.65% today, giving back some of yesterday's sharp 1.3% gain, even as crude oil prices held relatively steady near $102 a barrel. The decline appears to reflect profit-taking after the stock surged 13.5% over the past two weeks on the back of Middle East tensions and supply concerns—yesterday's pop to $484.92 on escalating Iran attacks in the Strait of Hormuz may have simply been the peak of that rally as traders locked in gains.

The broader refining backdrop remains supportive: refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, oil storage is moderate, and the recent announcement of a massive 20+ million barrel diesel release from the International Energy Agency suggests demand pressure (and pricing power) that refiners benefit from. But today's pullback signals that even with geopolitical risk priced in, the market is reassessing how much higher the stock can climb from here after its two-week surge.
